theory.overview: Building on basic graph traversal, this chapter covers advanced BFS/DFS techniques and applications. BFS excels at finding shortest paths in unweighted graphs and level-order processing. DFS is powerful for exploring all paths, cycle detection, and backtracking. Advanced topics include bidirectional BFS, iterative deepening DFS, topological sorting, and detecting cycles in directed graphs. These techniques form the foundation for more complex graph algorithms.

sections.title: Bidirectional BFS
sections.content: Simultaneous BFS from source and target. When frontiers meet, path found. Reduces search space from $O(b^d)$ to $O(2b^{d/2})$ where b is branching factor, d is depth. Useful for unweighted shortest path when both source and target known. Implementation: two queues, two visited sets. Alternate between expanding each frontier. Check for intersection.

sections.title: Iterative Deepening DFS (IDDFS)
sections.content: DFS with increasing depth limit. For depth limit L, run DFS limited to L. If target not found, increment L and repeat. Combines DFS's space efficiency ($O(d)$) with BFS's completeness. Time: $O(b^d)$. Space: $O(d)$. Useful when solution depth unknown and memory is limited.
sections.algorithm: For L from 0 to ∞: DFS with depth limit L. If target found, return.

sections.title: Topological Sort
sections.content: Linear ordering of vertices in DAG such that for every directed edge u→v, u comes before v. Used for task scheduling, build dependencies. Two methods: DFS (post-order, reverse result) and Kahn's algorithm (BFS with in-degree). Detects cycles: if not all vertices in topological order, cycle exists.

sections.title: Cycle Detection
sections.content: Undirected: DFS, if neighbor visited and not parent, cycle exists. Directed: DFS with three states (unvisited, visiting, visited). If edge to visiting node, back edge → cycle. Or Kahn's algorithm (if not all processed, cycle). Union-Find also detects cycles in undirected graphs.

methods.check: DFS, neighbor visited and not parent

sections.title: BFS Level Applications
sections.content: BFS naturally processes by level. Applications: shortest path in unweighted graph, minimum steps to reach target, level-order tree traversal, counting nodes at each level, finding minimum mutations. Key insight: first time visiting node = shortest distance from source.

keyConcepts.name: Bidirectional Search
keyConcepts.description: BFS from both ends simultaneously. Meets in middle. Dramatically reduces search space for large depths.

keyConcepts.name: Topological Order
keyConcepts.description: Linear ordering respecting edge directions. Only possible for DAGs. Multiple valid orders possible.
keyConcepts.property: If edge u→v, u appears before v in order

keyConcepts.name: Back Edge
keyConcepts.description: Edge to ancestor in DFS tree indicates cycle in directed graph. Edge to visited non-ancestor is cross edge (no cycle).

keyConcepts.name: In-Degree
keyConcepts.description: Number of edges entering vertex. Used in Kahn's algorithm for topological sort. Nodes with 0 in-degree can be processed first.
keyConcepts.kahn: Process nodes with 0 in-degree, decrement neighbors' in-degree

steps.title: Bidirectional BFS - Initialize
steps.description: Two queues: forward from source, backward from target. Two visited sets.

steps.title: Expand Frontier
steps.description: Alternate expanding each frontier. Check for intersection (node in both visited sets).
steps.code: while forwardQ and backwardQ: expand_forward(); if intersect: return; expand_backward(); if intersect: return;

steps.title: Check Intersection
steps.description: If any node in forwardVis is in backwardVis, paths meet. Reconstruct path.

steps.title: Topological Sort - DFS
steps.description: DFS, add node to result after processing all children. Reverse result at end.
steps.code: def dfs(node): mark visiting; for child: if not visited: dfs(child); result.append(node);

steps.title: Cycle Detection
steps.description: In directed DFS, if edge to visiting node, cycle found. Return false.
steps.code: if state[neighbor] == VISITING: return False; # cycle

practiceProblems.title: Word Ladder II
practiceProblems.description: Find all shortest transformation sequences from beginWord to endWord.
practiceProblems.solution: BFS level by level. Build parent map. At end, DFS from endWord to beginWord using parent map to reconstruct all paths.
practiceProblems.hints: BFS level by level, parent map, reconstruct paths

practiceProblems.title: Minimum Genetic Mutation
practiceProblems.description: Find minimum mutations to transform start to end using bank.
practiceProblems.solution: BFS from start. Each level = one mutation. Return level when reach end.

practiceProblems.title: Open the Lock
practiceProblems.description: Find minimum turns to open lock with 4 wheels given deadends.
practiceProblems.solution: BFS from '0000'. 8 possible moves per state. Skip deadends. Return steps when target reached.

practiceProblems.title: Shortest Path in Binary Matrix
practiceProblems.description: Find shortest path from top-left to bottom-right in binary matrix (8 directions).
practiceProblems.solution: BFS from (0,0). Queue stores (row, col, distance). Return distance when reach target.

practiceProblems.title: Shortest Bridge
practiceProblems.description: Find shortest bridge (flip 0 to 1) to connect two islands.
practiceProblems.solution: DFS to find first island, mark cells and add to queue. BFS from island to find nearest cell of second island.
practiceProblems.hints: DFS to find island, BFS to find second

practiceProblems.title: Nearest Exit from Entrance
practiceProblems.description: Find nearest exit from entrance in maze (4 directions).
practiceProblems.solution: BFS from entrance. Queue stores (row, col, distance). Return distance when reach border.

practiceProblems.title: As Far from Land as Possible
practiceProblems.description: Find water cell with maximum distance to nearest land.
practiceProblems.solution: Multi-source BFS from all land cells. Track distance. Max distance is answer.

practiceProblems.title: 01 Matrix
practiceProblems.description: For each cell, find distance to nearest 0.
practiceProblems.solution: Multi-source BFS from all 0s. Set distance = current + 1.

practiceProblems.title: Walls and Gates
practiceProblems.description: Fill each empty room with distance to nearest gate.
practiceProblems.solution: BFS from all gates. Update distance if current + 1 < existing.

practiceProblems.title: Course Schedule II
practiceProblems.description: Return ordering of courses to finish all (topological sort).
practiceProblems.solution: Topological sort using DFS or Kahn's. Return order if no cycle.

practiceProblems.title: Alien Dictionary
practiceProblems.description: Determine order of characters in alien language from sorted words.
practiceProblems.solution: Build graph from word comparisons. Topological sort. If cycle, invalid.
practiceProblems.hints: Build graph from word pairs, topological sort

practiceProblems.title: Sequence Reconstruction
practiceProblems.description: Check if sequence is unique topological order of graph.
practiceProblems.solution: Topological sort using Kahn's. If queue ever has >1 node, multiple orders possible.

practiceProblems.title: Course Schedule III
practiceProblems.description: Find minimum time to finish all courses with durations and prerequisites.
practiceProblems.solution: Topological sort with priority queue. Process by longest path time.
practiceProblems.hints: Topological sort with max-heap by time

practiceProblems.title: Parallel Courses
practiceProblems.description: Find minimum semesters to finish courses with prerequisites.
practiceProblems.solution: Topological sort (Kahn's). Count levels (semesters).

practiceProblems.title: Find Eventual Safe States
practiceProblems.description: Find nodes that eventually reach terminal node in directed graph.
practiceProblems.solution: Reverse graph, BFS from terminals. Nodes reachable in reverse are safe.

practiceProblems.title: Critical Connections
practiceProblems.description: Find critical connections (bridges) in network.
practiceProblems.solution: Tarjan's algorithm. Track discovery and low times. Bridge if low[child] > disc[node].
practiceProblems.hints: Tarjan's algorithm, discovery and low times

practiceProblems.title: Detect Cycles in Directed Graph
practiceProblems.description: Detect cycle in directed graph.
practiceProblems.solution: DFS with 3 states. If edge to visiting node, cycle. Or Kahn's (if not all processed, cycle).

practiceProblems.title: Find if Path Exists in Graph
practiceProblems.description: Check if path exists from source to destination.
practiceProblems.solution: BFS/DFS from source. Check if destination reached.

practiceProblems.title: All Paths from Source to Target
practiceProblems.description: Find all paths from source to target in DAG.
practiceProblems.solution: DFS with backtracking. Track current path. Add to result when target reached.

practiceProblems.title: Longest Increasing Path in Matrix
practiceProblems.description: Find longest increasing path in matrix.
practiceProblems.solution: DFS with memoization. Cache longest path from each cell.

practiceProblems.title: Word Search II
practiceProblems.description: Find all words from dictionary that exist in board (can move in 8 directions).
practiceProblems.solution: Build Trie from dictionary. DFS from each cell, traverse Trie. Remove word from Trie when found.

practiceProblems.title: Reconstruct Itinerary
practiceProblems.description: Reconstruct itinerary in lexical order given tickets.
practiceProblems.solution: Hierholzer's algorithm (Eulerian path). DFS, remove edges, add to result in reverse.

practiceProblems.title: Cracking the Safe
practiceProblems.description: Find shortest string that contains all n-length combinations of digits 0-k.
practiceProblems.solution: Hierholzer's algorithm on de Bruijn graph. Each node is n-1 digits, edge is digit.

practiceProblems.title: Shortest Path Visiting All Nodes
practiceProblems.description: Find shortest path visiting all nodes in undirected graph.
practiceProblems.solution: BFS on state (node, visited_mask). State space = node × all visited subsets.

practiceProblems.title: Minimum Height Trees
practiceProblems.description: Find roots of minimum height trees (MHTs) in undirected graph.
practiceProblems.solution: Topological sort from leaves (nodes with degree 1). Remove leaves layer by layer until ≤2 nodes remain.
